title: Canonical boundary projection components and comparison square
statement:
Let $C$ be a Grothendieck abelian closed symmetric monoidal coefficient category with additive tensor product and functorial flat resolutions, and assume the etale, pro-etale and comparison inverse images preserve flat objects. Use ordinary derived categories on small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For $i:Z\to T$ write $C_W=\nu_W^*$, $F_e=Ri_{e,*}$, $F_p=Ri_{p,*}$, $s_e=Li_e^*$, $s_p=Li_p^*$, $\rho:s_pC_T\cong C_Zs_e$, and $b:C_TF_e\to F_pC_Z$ for the canonical pullback square and its ordinary-adjunction direct-image mate [def-weil-boundary-exceptional-comparison-data]. For etale $B$ on $Z$ and $M$ on $T$, put $Q=B\otimes^Ls_eM$. Let $c_{W;K,L}:C_W(K\otimes^LL)\cong C_WK\otimes^LC_WL$ be the canonical monoidal comparison, with exactly the orientation inverse to the tensor comparison used to define the evaluation-Hom arrow [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison]. Define $\pi_e:F_eB\otimes^LM\to F_eQ$ and $\pi_p:F_pC_ZB\otimes^LC_TM\to F_p(C_ZB\otimes^Ls_pC_TM)$ to be the actual ordinary-counit-defined projection components [def-kun-projection-formula-map], on the respective sites.

Define $h:C_ZQ\cong C_ZB\otimes^Ls_pC_TM$ by $c_Z$ followed by $1\otimes\rho_M^{-1}$. For isomorphisms $b_B:C_TF_eB\cong F_pC_ZB$ and $b_Q:C_TF_eQ\cong F_pC_ZQ$, define $u:C_T(F_eB\otimes^LM)\cong F_pC_ZB\otimes^LC_TM$ by $c_T$ followed by $b_B\otimes1$, and $v:C_TF_eQ\cong F_p(C_ZB\otimes^Ls_pC_TM)$ by $b_Q$ followed by $F_p(h)$. Define the projection-comparison property to mean: $Q$ is bounded below; there exist such $b_B,b_Q$ with hom exactly $b$ at $B,Q$; and
$$v^{-1}\circ\pi_p=C_T(\pi_e)\circ u^{-1}.$$
In addition, for every isomorphism $e:F_eB\otimes^LM\cong F_eQ$ with $e.\mathrm{hom}=\pi_e$, there exists an isomorphism $e_p$ with hom $\pi_p$ and
$$e_p^{-1}\circ v=u\circ C_T(e^{-1}).$$
This defines a property of the canonical arrows and a conditional inverse square; it asserts neither that the property holds nor unconditional invertibility.
